outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Efficient Adaptation of Foundation Models
outline.description: The landscape of artificial intelligence has undergone a seismic shift with the advent of large foundation models. Recent architectures, such as ChatGPT for natural language processing and Stable Diffusion for image generation, have demonstrated remarkable generalization abilities across a vast array of domains. These models possess an unprecedented capacity to learn complex patterns from massive datasets, enabling them to perform tasks ranging from creative writing to sophisticated visual synthesis. However, this surge in performance is inextricably linked to a dramatic increase in scale. Modern foundation models often contain billions of parameters; for instance, GPT-3 boasts approximately 175 billion parameters. outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: An Information Transmission Framework for Matrix Factorization
outline.description: Before we can appreciate the novelty of the information transmission framework, we must first establish the foundational mechanics of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT). The core challenge in adapting large foundation models lies in updating the massive weight matrices without destroying the rich semantic knowledge acquired during pretraining. Standard approaches like Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) address this by adding a low-rank update matrix to the pretrained weights. In contrast, OFT adopts a multiplicative strategy. Instead of adding a perturbation, OFT reparameterizes the new weight matrix as the product of a learnable orthogonal matrix and the frozen pretrained weight matrix. outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: The Butterfly Structure and Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT)
outline.description: Having established the information transmission framework in the previous chapter, we now turn our attention to the central innovation of this work: Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT). The primary challenge identified was the inefficiency of traditional Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT), which relies on block-diagonal structures that impose rigid sparsity patterns and fail to capture the rich interactions between all neurons in a layer. While OFT preserves pairwise angles between neurons—a crucial property for retaining pre-trained knowledge—the cost of maintaining a fully dense orthogonal matrix scales quadratically with the dimension $d$, requiring $\mathcal{O}(d^2)$ parameters.
